html:
The Mexicaneros are a small Nahua people of the Sierra Madre Occidental where Durango meets Nayarit in western Mexico, living in villages such as San Pedro Jícoras and Santa Cruz de Acaponeta. They speak Mexicanero, a form of Nahuatl.

Whether their language was brought north by Nahua allies of the Spanish in the colonial period, or was spoken there earlier, is still debated. They live among the Huichol, Cora and Tepehuán, and share with them the mitote, a ceremonial dance for the maize harvest. They number about a thousand.
